summary: The paper proposes a single-location regression (SLR) task as a principled theoretical framework to explain softmax attention's empirical advantage over linear/kernelized alternatives in retrieval settings. Using statistical-physics tools (order parameters, replica method), the authors prove softmax attains Bayes risk in the population limit while linear attention fundamentally falls short, characterize other activations (erf, softplus), and provide a finite-sample high-dimensional characterization of the ERM via self-consistent equations. The analysis is technically substantive and addresses a genuinely under-theorized question, though the model is stylized (single-token, no query vector, one layer) and the finite-sample result relies on the non-rigorous replica method and a heuristic 'manifold' restriction.
strengths: Tackles a well-motivated and under-theorized question: why softmax dominates in retrieval-like tasks, with Figure 1 giving clear empirical motivation.
Clean formalization: SLR unifies spiked-SLR and max-SLR under a reweighted-Gaussian model, generalizing prior sequence multi-index results to variable sequence length.
Proposition 4.2 (softmax attains Bayes risk under a mild condition on g_nu including both variants studied) is a crisp and pleasing theoretical result, tied to the Nishimori condition.

Corollaries 4.3–4.4 make the softmax vs. linear separation quantitative in ν and L regimes; the analysis of how sequence-length variability specifically hurts linear attention is a nice mechanistic insight.

Extension beyond the population level to the proportional high-dimensional finite-sample regime (Result 5.1) with self-consistent equations, plus numerical agreement between the replica prediction and quasi-Newton ERM (Fig. 3), gives a coherent statistical + computational picture.
Limitations (absence of query vectors, non-rigor of replica, manifold restriction, possible bad local minima) are stated openly rather than buried.

key_concerns.issue: Result 5.1, the paper's main finite-sample statement, is explicitly derived by the non-rigorous replica method and additionally simplified via a manifold (diagonal order parameters) assumption whose validity outside softmax is only supported numerically or via a local-minimality argument. The paper's claim of a 'statistical advantage' at finite α therefore rests on two unproven pillars stacked together.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: State more precisely the scope of Result 5.1 (replica-symmetric, on-manifold prediction whose agreement with numerics is empirical), and either sketch how a replicon-condition proof would proceed for this specific two-index case or provide additional numerical robustness (multiple initializations, off-manifold perturbations, larger D) showing the on-manifold ERM is the true global minimum across the reported (ν, L, α) grid.

key_concerns.issue: Breadth/generality is thin relative to the framing. The paper motivates itself via LLM retrieval (Fig. 1, NIAH, MQAR) but the model has: one attention layer, no learnable query, Gaussian tokens, one relevant token per sequence, small deterministic or lightly-varying L (2, 3, 10 in figures), and evaluates only two activations analytically plus two numerically. The leap from 'softmax > linear on SLR at L=2,3,10' to explaining Fig. 1's LLM-scale retrieval gap is largely rhetorical.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Either tone down the LLM-motivation language in the introduction/conclusion, or add experiments at substantially larger L (e.g. L in the hundreds/thousands as in NIAH), varying token distributions, and ideally a multi-query variant closer to MQAR, to test whether the predicted gap scales as claimed.

key_concerns.issue: Baselines for the finite-sample section are narrow. Fig. 3 compares only linear vs. softmax; the erf and softplus-kernelized attentions studied in Section 4 (and referenced as important for isolating what property of softmax matters) are not carried into the finite-sample analysis. Without these, it is hard to attribute the finite-α gap to 'softmax' rather than to 'any well-normalized nonlinearity'.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Extend Result 5.1's numerical evaluation (or an ERM benchmark) to at least normalized-softplus and erf attention, so readers can see whether the statistical advantage is specifically softmax's or a broader normalization/tail-behavior effect.

key_concerns.issue: Experimental reporting on Figs. 2–3 does not describe seeds, error bars, or variance across draws of (k*, v*, dataset), and the caption mentions grid-searched regularizers without stating the search protocol or confidence in the reported minima.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report mean ± std over multiple seeds for the numerical curves, and state how many seeds/random initializations were used both for the fixed-point iterations and the quasi-Newton runs; the caption should point to the appendix where the grid and CIs are documented.

key_concerns.issue: Corollary 4.2 (uniqueness of the minimizer on M for linear attention, and its local-minimality in the full space) is used to justify convergence of GD to the on-manifold minimizer, but the paper also states elsewhere that the landscape has other local minima outside M. The reader is left uncertain how strongly the population-risk conclusion for linear attention generalizes.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Clarify explicitly what is proven (unique local minimum on M, local minimum in the full space) vs. what is conjectured (SGD from random init converges to it) and quantify empirically how often SGD escapes M in finite D.

key_concerns.issue: Clarity: the manuscript is very notation-dense, with many order parameters (mkk, mvv, Rkk, Rvv, qk, qv, Vk, Vv, mk, mv…) reused with subtle re-definitions between Sections 4 and 5. A reader who is not already versed in sequence multi-index / replica computations will struggle to keep the objects straight.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a compact notation table (or extend Table 1) mapping each order parameter to its physical meaning and where it first appears, and briefly recap in Section 5 which of the parameters from Section 4 survive and which are new.

key_concerns.issue: The 'connection with optimization by gradient-based algorithms' promised in the abstract is largely restricted to arguing (via Corollary 4.1 and empirical checks) that random init lands on M and GD stays there. There is no formal SGD sample-complexity result along the lines of Ben Arous et al. (2021), which the paper itself invokes.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Either downgrade the abstract's phrasing about optimization or add at least an informative-exponent / staircase-style discussion of one-pass SGD sample complexity for the SLR task under softmax vs. linear.

questions_for_authors: Does the softmax > linear separation persist when L is scaled with D (e.g. L = Θ(D^β)) rather than fixed at 2, 3, or 10? The high-dimensional limit is taken with D → ∞ at fixed L, which is arguably the least favorable regime for retrieval intuitions.

How sensitive is Result 5.1's numerical prediction to the diagonal/manifold simplification? Have you tried the full (non-diagonal) replica equations at least at one representative (ν, L, α) to check that off-diagonal order parameters vanish at the fixed point?

Corollary 4.3 shows Elin ~ 1/ν as ν → ∞ for spiked-SLR while Esoftmax decays exponentially. Do you observe the same rate separation at finite α in Result 5.1, or does the ν→∞, α finite regime introduce new phenomena (e.g. hard/easy phases as hinted at in the Bayes-optimal discussion)?

The absence of learnable query vectors is presented as innocuous via a [CLS]-token argument. Do numerical experiments with a full attention layer (learnable Q, K, V) reproduce the same softmax vs. linear ordering on SLR at the same (N, D, L)?

What is the behavior for erf and softplus-kernelized attention at finite α? Do they interpolate monotonically between linear and softmax as in the population case, or does the ordering change with sample complexity?

Fig. 3 reports agreement between quasi-Newton ERM and Result 5.1 at √(ND) = 10^4. Does the agreement degrade in the small-α, high-regularization regime, and if so, is this attributable to bad local minima or to breakdown of replica symmetry?
calibration_check: Claims are mostly appropriately scoped — softmax = Bayes only proved in population and only under the stated g_nu condition, Result 5.1 openly labeled non-rigorous — but the introduction/abstract's framing that this explains softmax's empirical dominance in LLM retrieval is broader than the SLR evidence actually supports.

significance.justification: A principled theoretical account of why softmax beats linear/kernelized attention on retrieval-like tasks is a question the community actively cares about; the Bayes-optimality and quantitative gap results are the kind of insight ICLR readers would cite, though the toy model limits immediate practical uptake.

novelty.justification: The SLR formalization with variable sequence lengths, the g_nu-condition under which softmax attains Bayes risk, and the finite-α self-consistent equations for a two-index softmax model are new relative to the cited sequence multi-index literature, though the methodology heavily builds on existing statistical-physics machinery and concurrent work (Dohmatob 2025, Dragutinović 2025, Barnfield 2026) explores nearby territory.

rigor.justification: Population-level results (Prop. 4.1–4.4, Cor. 4.1–4.4) appear rigorous with proofs deferred to the appendix, but the flagship finite-sample Result 5.1 is explicitly non-rigorous (replica method), is further restricted by a heuristic manifold assumption, and the landscape claims are only partial.

statistical_soundness.justification: The 'statistical soundness' here is theoretical (replica + fixed-point); numerical validation in Figs. 2–3 looks reasonable but reported without seeds, error bars, or variance across (k*, v*) draws in the captions, which is standard for this literature but weak by ICLR empirical norms.

calibration_honesty.justification: The paper is unusually candid about its assumptions: non-rigor of the replica method, manifold restriction, absence of query vectors, existence of other local minima, and left-for-future-work items are all stated explicitly, though the abstract/intro framing vs. LLM retrieval is slightly overreached.

clarity.justification: The task, high-level story, and main propositions are stated clearly, but the notation load is heavy (many order parameters, redefinitions across sections) and key results like (17)–(25) are difficult to parse without significant appendix reference.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard conference structure (Intro, Related Work, Task/Data, Population Analysis, Finite-Sample Analysis) with appropriate use of appendices; length appears within ICLR norms.

reproducibility.justification: The probabilistic data model, activation choices, order parameters, and self-consistent equations are described in enough detail that a competent reader could reimplement; hyperparameter grid and simulation details are said to be in the appendix, and code is mentioned as provided (URL removed per anonymization).

related_work.justification: Related work is broad and fair — kernelized attention, SSMs, linear-attention theory, associative recall / MQAR, sequence multi-index framework, and concurrent papers (Dohmatob, Dragutinović, Barnfield) are all placed in context; positioning against Marion et al. and Troiani et al. is explicit.

figure_quality.justification: Fig. 1 (reproduced from Shen et al.) motivates the question well; Fig. 2 cleanly sweeps ν across four activations and two tasks under varying L, directly supporting the linear-vs-softmax-vs-normalization story; Fig. 3 shows theory-vs-ERM agreement across three tasks and ν values — the display items match the claims, though captions could report seeds/errors.

breadth_generality.justification: The paper's claimed motivation is LLM-scale retrieval, but empirical/theoretical support covers one attention layer, no query vector, Gaussian tokens, small L (2, 3, 10), one relevant token, and finite-sample experiments only for linear vs. softmax (not erf/softplus); the leap to real retrieval is under-supported.

overall_recommendation.justification: Borderline accept: a solid, honestly-scoped theoretical contribution with a clean Bayes-optimality result and coherent finite-sample story, but limited breadth, reliance on non-rigorous replica machinery, and a manifold assumption that isn't fully validated keep it from being a clear-accept.
